case_selection_policy: Uses every runnable case in the default forensic statistical benchmark corpus as of 2026-05-22. Expected and contradictory axes are inherited from the curated statistical fixtures; this ASC-ruler fixture only fixes the case list and records why each case belongs in the validation set.
primary_target: ASC ruler house placement risk-tone context support

source_doctrine_cases.source_note: McIntosh states that the victim ruler in the 1st can show the person has not been taken, may have voluntarily left, or that the perpetrator was in the victim's vicinity, residence, or in front of them.
McIntosh states that if the ruler of the victim is in the 2nd house, consider whether the person was taken for trafficking because the second house makes the person a possession in this instance.
McIntosh states that the 3rd house can imply a communication problem, verbal argument, siblings or cousins, vehicles, and short distance.
McIntosh states that the 4th house points first toward family and is serious as the house of the end of the matter, womb and tomb.
McIntosh states that the 5th house can show the person was in a situation of partying, drinking, dancing, entertainment, or being out having fun.
McIntosh states that the 6th house shows the victim doing their routine normal thing when disrupted by another person and can imply a stalker or watcher.
McIntosh states that the victim ruler in the 7th puts the victim in front of the suspect and most likely on the suspect's territory or comfort zone.
McIntosh states that the 8th house immediately suggests looking for a deceased person and can also show financial disagreement, inheritance, or debts.
McIntosh states that the 9th house shows the victim is likely far away or going further away at the point of reading the chart.
McIntosh states that the 10th house implies the story becomes public, out in the open, likely seen by a witness, and shows authorities, police, government, boss, or parents.
McIntosh states that the 11th house indicates the victim may have been surrounded by or with friends, friends may know what happened, and hopes and dreams were taken away.
McIntosh states that the 12th house can show the victim may not be found, may be in an enclosed area, hidden and kept hidden, or kidnapped.

Tenant double homicide and concealment case; validates fatal-pressure placement against homicide and deception labels.
